description.summary: the compositor's channel to its settings app

protocol.description:
What perspicax-settings needs from the compositor that no standard protocol carries: the next chord the person presses, as the compositor reads it, so that the app can bind it.
A binding is matched inside the compositor, before any client sees the key. A client listening on wl_keyboard would never hear a chord that is already bound: pressing Logo+Return to rebind it would start a terminal instead. And the compositor matches a key by several keysyms at once, under every layout in the keymap, which a client reading its own keymap cannot be sure of reproducing. So the compositor reports the press itself, with the keysyms it matches a binding by, and the client spells the chord from those.
The global is privileged: the compositor offers it only to the programs its [protocols] settings rule admits. While the session is locked nothing is captured.

interface.name: perspicax_settings_v1

description.summary: a settings app's binding to the compositor

interface.description: Bound once by the settings app.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The client is done with this object. A capture it asked for is left as it is, and is destroyed on its own.

request.name: capture_chord
request.description:
Wait for the next chord the person presses while a surface of this client's process has the keyboard. The process, not this connection: a toolkit that keeps its own connection draws the window, and the capture is asked for on another.
One capture waits at a time, whoever asked: a new one replaces the one waiting, which is cancelled as replaced. One asked for while no surface of this process has the keyboard, or while the session is locked, is cancelled at once.

interface.name: perspicax_chord_capture_v1
interface.description:
Exactly one of chord, tap, hatch or cancelled is sent, and then nothing more. The client destroys the object once it has heard.
While it waits, keys reach the focused surface as ever, but for the one that makes the chord: a modifier on its own is pressed and let go as usual, so the client can show what is held, while the key pressed with them is taken, its release too, and neither a binding nor any client sees it. The escape hatches are still what they are.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The client is done with this capture. If it still waits, it waits no more, and the next chord is matched against the bindings as any other.

enum.name: mods
enum.description: Caps Lock and Num Lock are not among them: a binding never depends on them.

entry.name: vt
entry.summary: Ctrl+Alt+F1 to F12, which switch VT

entry.name: unfocused
entry.summary: no surface of the asking process has the keyboard

entry.name: withdrawn
entry.summary: the [protocols] settings rule no longer admits this client

event.name: chord

description.summary: a key was pressed with these modifiers

event.description:
A key pressed with mods held. The other arguments are the keysyms a binding finds the key by, which the compositor tries in this order, the first that is bound winning:
made, what the key made with the modifiers held; raw, what it makes with none in the layout in use, as an array of 32-bit keysyms in the host's byte order; latin, what it makes in the keymap's first layout with a Latin letter on it, so that Logo+q pressed under a Cyrillic layout is Logo+q; shifted, what it makes with Shift in the layout in use, which counts only when it is a digit, as on an AZERTY number row.
Zero is no keysym.

arg.name: made
arg.summary: the keysym made with them held

arg.name: latin
arg.summary: the keysym in the Latin layout, or 0

arg.name: shifted
arg.summary: the keysym made with Shift, or 0

event.name: tap
event.description: The Logo key was pressed and let go with nothing else in between, which a binding written "Logo" takes. Its press and release still reached the client.

event.name: hatch
event.description: One of the chords no configuration can take away was pressed, and is done once this is sent: the session ends, or the VT switches. It cannot be bound.

arg.name: vt
arg.summary: for vt, the VT counted from 1; 0 for exit

event.name: cancelled

description.summary: the capture ended with no chord

event.description: Nothing was captured, for this reason.
